      - article:
        - heading "2 Notice the Pattern" [level=3]
        - paragraph: • Straight-line has equal annual depreciation.
        - paragraph: • Reducing-balance has larger depreciation early and smaller later.
        - paragraph: • Both methods are decreasing and never negative.

      - article:
        - heading "▥ Understand the Rule" [level=3]
        - paragraph: "Definitions Book value after t years: value of asset after t complete years of depreciation."
        - paragraph:
          - text: "Key Rules Straight-line: B"
          - subscript: SL
          - text: "(t) = P - ((P-S)/n)t Reducing-balance: B"
          - subscript: RB
          - text: (t) = P(1-r)
          - superscript: t
      - article:
        - heading "⊙ Common Misconception" [level=3]
        - paragraph: "Mistake: Assuming reducing-balance also ends at the residual value S."
        - paragraph: "Reality: It approaches S but may not reach it exactly; a switch method is used in practice."
        - img
        - complementary: Takeaway Reducing-balance preserves more value in the later years compared to straight-line.
      - article:
        - heading "✎ Try Independently" [level=3]
        - paragraph: "Change the rate r or life n. Explain:"
        - paragraph: 1. How does a higher r affect early depreciation?
        - paragraph: 2. For which method does more value remain in late years?
      - article:
        - heading "☆ Challenge (One Step Further)" [level=3]
        - paragraph: An asset costs ₹120,000, residual value ₹10,000, life 6 years, reducing-balance rate 20%.

        - complementary: Answer ₹61,440.00
